text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

Hello A,

I am helping all three of you talk through a plan for the house and the will. I am sorry about your dad. I am sending the same note to A, B, and C. I cannot make legal decisions or move money. Please do not sign anything yet.

Please reply with your concerns, what you want, and any deadline. A, please confirm what you and your husband propose. B, please tell me what money you need and when. C, please tell me what would work for you. If you need more time, say so. I will not treat silence as agreement.

Here is the current list, which I will keep in the same part of every update to all three of you so everyone can find it quickly.

I’d like some money to help me start a dance studio, though I’m not sure yet what amount or timing would be realistic. I have no firm deadline. I’m a little concerned about agreeing to a discounted sale before we’ve talked everything through, so I’d rather not sign anything yet.

Hello C,

I am sorry about your dad. I sent the opening note to A and B. I am sending it to you now with the current list. I am helping all three of you find a plan for the house and the will. I cannot make legal decisions or move money. Please do not sign anything yet.

I have heard from A and B. The main point is that no one should sign anything yet. A says no price or deadline is settled, and B wants more time to talk things through.

Here is a short plan for all three of you. First, pause any sale or signing. Second, ask A and her husband for a clear written offer with the proposed amount, timing, and reason for any discount. Third, get an independent view of the house's current value. Fourth, ask a lawyer to explain the will and any steps that need signatures. Fifth, ask B to name a realistic amount and timing for the dance studio. Sixth, ask C to say what would work for her. Finally, wait for A, B, and C to agree in writing after legal advice before any sale or discount.

Please reply with your concerns, goals, and any deadline. C, please tell me what would work for you, and name any deadline. Please reply when you can. If you need more time, say so. I will not treat silence as agreement.

Here is the current list. I will keep this same list at the end of every update to all three of you so everyone can find it quickly.

Thanks. I want a fair financial share and won’t subsidize A’s discounted purchase; I haven’t agreed to it. An independent valuation and legal advice make sense. I have no deadline and am not in a hurry, but I’d like this settled fairly.
